findings.text: Boot namespace setup provides an init-time entry honoring an optional pre-mount delay, ensuring settled device discovery, initializing stacked volume assembly, resolving a saved root name, staging legacy ramdisk content, optionally blocking for late root arrival, mounting the resolved root with device nodes, then pivoting into the new root and detaching the old one while reporting pivot or detach failures.

Root waiting becomes a no-op once a root identifier is already assigned. Otherwise it announces the awaited name, derives a deadline from a configurable wait interval, polls probe completion plus name lookup with a short sleep until success or deadline expiry under a positive timeout, then synchronizes outstanding asynchronous work before returning.

Root name resolution dedicates distinct identifiers to prefix mtd, prefix ubi, path /dev/nfs, path /dev/cifs and path /dev/ram, delegating all other names to early block lookup. An invalid lookup outcome combined with an enabled wait clears the wait flag and yields an unset device.

Ramdisk staging offers two builds under one name. A header inline build does nothing. A full build conditionally instantiates node /dev/ram, loads an image while emitting a deprecation notice on success, and always removes staging path /initrd.image.

Full ramdisk image loading opens target /dev/ram plus source /initrd.image, determines extent and compression handling from the configured start offset, delegates compressed payloads to a dedicated decompression path, otherwise validates fit against target capacity, copies payload in fixed-size chunks with human progress indication, then releases resources, removes the ram alias, and reports success as an integer flag.
A header inline build of ramdisk image loading unconditionally reports absence of work with a zero result and performs no input output.

Image identification probes a 512-byte prefix at the configured start for compression signatures first, then checks base-offset markers for rom, cram and squash formats, retries cram after a 512-byte stride, then examines the following block for minix and extended filesystem markers. Allocation failure yields a memory error, compressed payloads yield zero, recognized filesystems yield a kilobyte-unit extent, and unrecognized content yields a generic failure.
Target capacity query yields zero for non-block inodes and otherwise converts cached size to kilobyte units through a ten-bit shift.

Compressed ramdisk loading treats a missing decompression handler as fatal and halts the boot. Otherwise it invokes the handler with shared fill plus flush adapters and a shared textual fault reporter, folding any recorded asynchronous fault flag into a failure result.

Root filesystem registration pairs a fixed textual name with context creation dispatch and anonymous superblock release. Context creation selects between shared-memory and ram backends under compile-time gating plus a runtime boolean selector.

A static boolean selector determines early root context behavior, choosing the shared-memory backend only when both compile-time support and the runtime flag agree, with the ram backend as the fallback.

Early ramdisk bookkeeping retains virtual start and end positions, a flag permitting placement below start, physical start plus size descriptors, and a default-enabled mount switch that a deprecated opt-out string clears while warning.
Early ramdisk memory parsing accepts a start value with an optional comma-separated size suffix, storing both into physical descriptors and ignoring absent size tails.

Ramdisk staging retains shared input and output handles with independent positions plus a configurable image origin defaulting to zero. A deprecated textual option overrides the origin through automatic-base integer parsing while warning.

Streaming decompression adapters share input and output positions plus fault markers. Fill reports read faults and unexpected end of input. Flush demands exact-length writes and latches a shared fault on shortfall. Textual faults latch both exit and decompression fault markers.

Primordial signal state describes single-threaded ownership linked to the initial task, initialized child-exit and shared pending queues, multiprocess linkage, default limits, guard mutex plus execution-update lock with optional cgroup and timer state, accounting hooks, and pid linkage for all roles to the initial pid object.

Primordial signal and handler objects arrive statically locked-ready with an initialized guard mutex, execution-update semaphore, optional cgroup semaphore, handler spin primitive and signalfd queue, establishing no runtime lock setup precedes first use.
Primordial handler table carries a single reference, default dispositions across all entries, an unlocked spin primitive, and an initialized signalfd wait queue.

Primordial credentials encode multiple references, root identities across all user and group fields, default secure bits, an empty inheritable set with full permitted effective and bounding sets, and linkage to initial user, namespace, group storage and usage counters.

Primordial execution support combines an execution state with two references, owner-only dumpability and initial user namespace, fixed shadow call storage terminated by a magic marker, group storage with two references, and a thread descriptor statically bound to the initial task.

Initramfs output fragments large transfers to respect a maximum write bound, retries transient interruptible failures, stops on other errors or zero progress, folds written bytes into a running checksum only during checksum mode, and returns the accumulated count.

Hardlink tracking uses a fixed small bucket array keyed by device major plus minor and inode number with file-type filtering, storing aligned pathname buffers sized from the path limit and a global observation marker.

Link lookup returns a prior pathname on matching device, inode and type bits, otherwise records the new name and marks observation. Table release frees all chains only after observation and then clears the marker.

Deferred directory timestamp handling maintains a doubly linked list of variable-length entries pairing modification times with names, allocated flexibly, queued at creation, then drained by stamping times and freeing each node.

Timestamp handling has dual builds. An active build stamps both access and modification times through pathname and open-file paths while maintaining a deferred directory queue. An empty build turns all timestamp plus queue operations into no-ops.

Archive header decoding translates thirteen hexadecimal textual fields after a six-character magic prefix into numeric inode, mode, ownership, link count, time, payload and name lengths, device numbers and checksum globals, noting a far-future time truncation limit and reporting damage on decode failure.

Initramfs extraction runs an eight-state machine across start, buffering collect, header validation, skip-ahead, name handling, file copy, symlink handling and padding reset, driven by cursor plus limit pointers with helpers to consume input, stage fixed reads, and compute aligned next-header offsets. It distinguishes checksum modes by magic, rejects unknown magics and invalid name lengths, and flags broken padding.

Entry creation validates nul termination and trailer completion, replaces mismatched existing types, reuses prior hardlink targets when link counts warrant, then branches by type to regular files with ownership mode truncation incremental copy plus optional checksum check, directories with deferred timestamps, special nodes with immediate timestamps, and symlinks with combined name plus target handling.
Hardlink hash exposes thirty-two buckets selected by a five-bit mask derived from inode plus minor plus shifted major with an additional folding shift.
Initramfs framing distinguishes checksum modes through magic 070701 versus magic 070702, reports method misuse on magic 070707, and terminates on trailer name TRAILER!!!.
Root filesystem type object is provided for early root mounting with a fixed name and anonymous superblock lifecycle.

Archive fault handling retains only the first textual fault message as sticky state, halts with a memory dump solely on hash or directory allocation failure, and otherwise records write, checksum, padding and format faults without immediate halt.
